question: Manish travels from City A to City B. If Manish drives his car at 1/3​ of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 36 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Manish would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio (Normal : New) = 3 : 1

Time ratio (Normal : New) = 1 : 3 (Since time is inversely proportional to speed)

Difference in time ratio = 3 − 1 = 2 units

2 units → 36 minutes late

1 unit (Normal time) → 18 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
• 
 
 City A
 City B
 Distance = D
 
 
 Normal: Speed = S
 Time = T min
 
 
 New: Speed = S / 3
 Time = (T + 36) min

**Given:**

New speed = 1/3 of normal speed

Time delay = 36 minutes late

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

When distance is constant, Speed × Time = Constant

**Calculation:**

Let the normal speed be S and normal time be T.

⇒ Normal distance = S × T

⇒ New speed = S / 3

⇒ New time = T + 36

Since the distance traveled is the same in both cases:

⇒ S × T = (S / 3) × (T + 36)

⇒ T = (T + 36) / 3

⇒ 3T = T + 36

⇒ 2T = 36

⇒ T = 18 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality of Speed and Time

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time. If speed is reduced to a/b of its original value, the time taken becomes b/a of the original time.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy / (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|. When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
